sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Portage County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Two offices in Ravenna split the work. The county auditor values every parcel and sets the rates, and the county treasurer sends the bills and takes the payments. A third body, the Board of Revision, hears valuation complaints, and the auditor acts as its secretary.

The county's own About Portage County page describes the auditor as the tax assessor for every political subdivision in the county and the treasurer as the collector of all tax money. It also says the treasurer sits on the Board of Revision. For a seller, that means one office answers valuation questions and another answers payment questions, so call the right one first.

The auditor's real estate search site, portagecountyauditor.org, offers parcel searches and a tax estimator by taxing district and property value. Pull your parcel there before you list so you know the figures a buyer's agent will see.

sections.h2: How is a Portage County tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The treasurer's tax rates page lays out the steps. The auditor finds fair market value, takes 35% of it as assessed value, then multiplies by the total mill rate and divides by 1,000. Every Ohio owner carries a base of 10 mills from the state constitution, and voter-approved levies for schools, roads, libraries and other services stack on top.

Special assessments, such as water lines, sewer lines and storm water systems, are added after that. Reduction credits come off the total last. Rates are recalculated every year, and the page links the published rate sheets for 2010 through the 2025 rates collected in 2026.

  • Fair market value is what a willing buyer and seller would agree to in an arm's length sale.
  • Assessed value in Ohio is 35% of that figure.
  • The total mill rate depends on which school district, township or city your parcel sits in.
  • Special assessments are billed in addition to the base tax.

The page lists the auditor's office at 330-297-3561 for questions about how rates are calculated. Use that number if your sheet and your bill do not match.

sections.h2: When are Portage County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The treasurer's page says taxes are collected twice a year, with about half due in February and the rest due in July. The July half is not always fixed on the calendar. In 2026 the Ohio Tax Commissioner moved the second-half deadline to September 9, because the new inflation cap credit under House Bill 186 delayed bill processing, and a county release said no interest or penalty would run before that date. That date has passed.

Because extensions like that can happen, check the treasurer's page for the printed due date on your own bill instead of counting on a calendar date from memory.

Late payment has a statutory price. Under R.C. 323.121, a ten percent penalty attaches to an unpaid half after its last payment date, and the treasurer waives half of that penalty when the full amount arrives within ten days. Interest then runs on delinquent amounts at the rate the Revised Code sets. If you are selling with a half unpaid, ask the title company to collect it from your proceeds at closing so no penalty starts.

sections.h2: Can I appeal a Portage County valuation before I sell?
sections.html:
Yes, but only inside a fixed window. The county's FAQ on disputed values says complaints are accepted by the auditor from January 1 through March 31 each year and are heard by the Board of Revision. A complaint has to reach the auditor, at P.O. Box 1217, Ravenna, OH 44266, by March 31.

The county's instruction sheet adds details that trip up owners:

  • The signature on the DTE 1 complaint form must be notarized, or the Board will not take it.
  • The Board looks at the current tax year only, not earlier years.
  • A complaint built on a sale has to show an arm's length deal. The sheet says foreclosure sales, sheriff sales, bank transactions and sales between family members are generally not treated as valid.
  • High taxes alone are not grounds, because the Board weighs value, not the bill.
  • Filing does not excuse payment on time. While a complaint is pending, you may tender the amount based on your claimed value, and interest applies on any shortfall.

If the stated change in assessed value is at least $17,500, the school board gets 30 days to file a counter-complaint, and no hearing is set until that time passes. The statute behind all of this is R.C. 5715.19, which also bars a second complaint in the same interim period unless a sale, casualty loss, major improvement or occupancy swing of 15 percent has changed things.

sections.h2: Which Portage County offices will I deal with in a sale?
sections.html:
A closing here touches the auditor, the treasurer and the recorder. The table gathers what each one printed for the public.

Portage County offices involved in a home sale, with details as published on the county and auditor sites
OfficeRolePublished contact
AuditorTransfers the deed, keeps values, takes valuation complaints449 South Meridian Street, Ravenna; appraisal (330) 297-3568; main (330) 297-3565
TreasurerBills and collects both halvesReached through the county site, portagecounty-oh.gov
RecorderRecords the deed and mortgage releasesMain office (330) 297-3553; fax (330) 297-7349

The auditor's transfer page says the real estate department transfers deeds before they are recorded, and prints a conveyance fee of $4.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel on the DTE 100 form. Ohio also allows a county to levy a separate transfer tax of up to 30 cents per $100 under R.C. 322.02, so ask the auditor whether one applies to your deed.

sections.h2: What is Portage County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Portage County sits in Northeast Ohio, with Ravenna as county seat and Kent as the largest city. Wikipedia names Kent, Ravenna, Aurora and Streetsboro as its cities, adds 18 civil townships, and puts the 2020 population at 161,791. The county covers 504 square miles, and 38% of residents live in rural areas.

The county's about page names Kent State University, Hiram College and Northeast Ohio Medical University among its schools, and it notes that Interstate 80, which includes the Ohio Turnpike, and Interstate 76 cross the county. The same Wikipedia entry reports 68.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied and 31.1% rented, a split that shapes who buys a house here.

Where your parcel sits changes the bill. A house in a city, a village school district or an unincorporated township carries a different mix of levies, so compare the rate sheet for your district rather than a countywide average.

sections.h2: What should a seller with back taxes ask for?
sections.html:
Start with a payoff request. Ask the treasurer for the amount owed on your parcel, including any delinquent years, penalty and interest, and give that figure to the closing agent. Ask the auditor whether any special assessment is attached, since those travel with the parcel.

  • Request a printout of the parcel's tax history from the auditor's real estate site.
  • Ask the treasurer whether a payment plan is open on the parcel.
  • Confirm with the title company how the current half will be split between you and the buyer.
  • Check for open valuation complaints, because a pending one can change what is owed.

Sellers who cannot clear the debt before a traditional listing can still sell. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, and the unpaid tax is paid from the price at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I file a property value complaint in Portage County?
faqs.a: File it with the Portage County Auditor, whose office is at 449 South Meridian Street in Ravenna, using the DTE 1 form, between January 1 and March 31. The Board of Revision hears it, and the signature on the form must be notarized.

faqs.q: What is the assessed value of a house in Portage County?
faqs.a: It is 35% of fair market value, according to the treasurer's rate page. The auditor then multiplies that figure by the total mill rate for your district and divides by 1,000.

faqs.q: Are Portage County tax bills paid in two parts?
faqs.a: Yes. The treasurer collects about half in February and the rest in July. In 2026 the second-half date was pushed to September 9, a date that has passed, so rely on the due date printed on your own bill.

faqs.q: What does Portage County charge to transfer a deed?
faqs.a: The auditor's page lists $4.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel. The recorder charges its own fee on top, and the state sets that schedule in R.C. 317.32.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Portage County house that owes taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount is taken from your proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure from the treasurer first. A buyer who purchases as-is does not need the debt cleared before the contract is signed.
